questions.summary: How the boot ROM starts MPC2000.EXE, where the EXE and SYS sit in physical memory, and how a modified SYS can be loaded and undone, are not established.

machines.summary: OS 1.72 (MPC2000.EXE and MPC2000.SYS) is identified by hash. Its address model, about 50 OS routines and software interrupts, in-RAM program, sequence and voice layouts and disk services are recorded: entry points checked against the bytes, meanings from a published mod source. Hardware, boot path and memory map are not documented. Nothing is hardware-tested here.

sources: NEC V53 user's manual (interrupt controller, timer unit)
findings.summary: How OS 1.20 code calls and is called, the inline-operand software interrupts, the interrupt controller and tick rules that keep a mod from freezing the machine, and five ways of hooking the OS that have run on hardware.
findings.title: Calling conventions, OS services and hook patterns proven on hardware

sources: NEC V53 user's manual (page registers, printed pp.67-71 and 121-123)
findings.summary: The OS runs from a RAM copy where segment × 16 + offset equals the file offset. This gives the address forms, the boot page-register map, and the run-time remapping of the top half of that copy that every mod must respect.
findings.title: How addresses work on the MPC2000XL (file, physical, runtime)

findings.summary: From the reset vector to the OS. The boot block sets up the V53, waits for the panel MCU to send the ID bytes E0 11, checks the OS image and copies it to RAM. An emulator must answer the ID wait to boot.
findings.title: Boot path and the panel ID handshake

findings.summary: Step-by-step route for changing OS 1.20 - patch a copy of the image, repair its checksum, check protected regions, flash it with the stock updater and keep a stock image ready to roll back. Each step has been done on hardware.
findings.title: Recipe: patch OS 1.20, flash it, and roll it back

findings.summary: OS 1.20 has no documented free space. Ranges that must never be written are listed with the reason. Room has been made by retiring features whose code is proven never to run; zero bytes alone do not make a range safe.
findings.title: Where added code can and cannot go in OS 1.20

findings.summary: Assemble for the 80186; 386 encodings fault on the V53A. Inline-operand interrupts, V53-only instructions and screen programs that mix code and data all break linear disassembly.
findings.title: Assembler and disassembler pitfalls on the MPC2000XL

findings.summary: Byte layouts of the .SND sound file (complete), the .PGM program file (framing and record layout) and the .ALL sequence container (framing), checked against files written by a real MPC2000XL and against the OS's loaders.
findings.title: SND, PGM and ALL file layouts

sources: Akai MPC2000XL main-board schematic (MAIN 1-3 and OPERATION sheets)
findings.summary: The chips on the MPC2000XL main and operation boards and what each one does, from the schematics, the user manual and board photographs.
findings.title: MPC2000XL hardware overview

findings.summary: Where the flash, RAM and every peripheral sit, the interrupt and DMA lines each uses, and how the OS programs them, from the schematics and the OS 1.20 code.
findings.title: MPC2000XL memory map, I/O ports, interrupts and DMA

findings.summary: The two MIDI outputs are the two channels of an MB89371A. The OS's enqueue routines take a status byte and data in registers, handle running status, and are safe to call from added code inside a short critical section. SIO2 drives MIDI OUT B on hardware.
findings.title: MIDI ports and how to send MIDI from added code

sources: vubeatz (Dariusz Chynek), mpc2000_2000xl_mod_pack at commit eb8ece6, mods/*.S (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0; facts restated, no code copied)
findings.summary: About 20 far routines in OS 1.20 (screen, editor, voice stop, DSP transfer, sample memory), INT 7Fh-EAh services, the in-RAM program and sound records and a 481-word pitch table at 582B:0056. Entries checked against the bytes; meanings from a mod source.
findings.title: OS 1.20 routines, software interrupts and RAM structures used by the vubeatz mods

findings.summary: Every key, pad, wheel and slider event reaches the main CPU as a two-byte report from the panel MCU; this gives each header and its handler. The 13 LEDs are written directly by the main CPU through two latches; each LED's port is confirmed on hardware.
findings.title: Front-panel input reports and the LED latches

findings.summary: The OS update file is the flat 512 KiB flash image. An update never writes the boot block, every cold boot checks a magic string and a word sum, and a failed image drops to a disk recovery loader rather than bricking the unit.
findings.title: The OS image, the flash update, the boot checksum and recovery

findings.summary: The five address forms used in this repository, how the V53 page registers turn a 20-bit address into a 24-bit one, and the three page tables the firmware loads.
findings.title: How addresses work on the MPC3000 (V53 extended addressing)

sources: MAME devices/video/hd61830 (register numbering used for comparison)
findings.summary: The BIOS in the top 32 KiB of the EPROM offers services through software interrupts. INT 43h writes text to the LCD, INT 41h reads files, INT 45h loads an MZ program.
findings.title: BIOS software-interrupt services (LCD text, files, program load)

findings.summary: Step-by-step route for running your own code on an MPC3000 from a floppy .SYS file, with a working minimal program, the rules it must obey, and how to test before touching a machine.
findings.title: Recipe: build and run your own program from floppy

findings.summary: OS application code is far cdecl (arguments pushed right to left, first argument at [BP+6], caller cleans up, RETF). The AMX kernel and the BIOS each use a different convention.
findings.title: Calling conventions used by the OS, kernel and BIOS

findings.summary: Common 8086 disassemblers mis-decode the V53 instructions BRKXA and RETXA and lose the instruction stream after them. Other traps are decoding one chip file alone and trusting raw opcode counts.
findings.title: Disassembler pitfalls on V53 firmware

findings.summary: The OS is two interleaved 256 KiB EPROMs. This gives the layout of the interleaved image, the reset path, and the rule that an image is identified by hash, never by the version it prints.
findings.title: MPC3000 OS EPROM layout and how to identify an image

findings.summary: At power-on every examined EPROM OS loads the first *.SYS file on a floppy as a DOS MZ executable into RAM and jumps to it. This is the only ROM path that runs code from removable media.
findings.title: The ROM floppy loader that runs a .SYS file at power-on

findings.summary: The chips on the MPC3000 CPU board and what each one does, taken from the Akai service parts list and the MAME driver.
findings.title: MPC3000 hardware overview

findings.summary: Which code owns each interrupt vector once the OS has started, who installs it, and how to install a handler the way the OS does.
findings.title: Interrupt vector table after boot

findings.summary: Where ROM, RAM, NVRAM and every peripheral sit, and which interrupt and DMA line each device uses, as modelled by the MAME driver.
findings.title: MPC3000 memory map, I/O ports, interrupts and DMA

findings.summary: On 3.12 and Vailixi 3.50 EPROMs stock OS 3.16 lets sequence data overwrite its own code and hangs at Song. With a SCSI disk its partition reader wraps the stack. Both causes and working fixes are described.
findings.title: Two memory defects in stock OS 3.16, and their fixes

findings.summary: Append a code segment to M3K316.SYS, extend its relocation table, move the new code above 3.16 at load time, and hook 3.16 by far jumps. Builds made this way run on real hardware.
findings.title: Recipe: add code to OS 3.16 and load it from floppy

findings.summary: OS 3.16 is a self-contained MZ program with its own BIOS and AMX kernel. This gives its layout, address forms, start-up, tasks, memory use and a map of 111 named routines and data objects.
findings.title: OS 3.16 (M3K316.SYS) structure, memory and named routines

findings.summary: Two blocks totalling 147,372 bytes of the 512 KiB image are empty and are not mapped by any of the firmware's page tables. Using them needs a page-table change; a smaller empty block inside the OS code range is directly reachable.
findings.title: Unused space in the OS EPROMs

sources: MPC3000 OS 3.40.0 Track Mute Edition README (English, PDF, Deep88, November 2026)
findings.summary: The OS 3.41 Track Mute Edition SYS file is OS 3.16 with changes. It has the same MZ layout, 95% of 3.16's load image is unchanged at the same offsets, and 103 of 108 pinned 3.16 ranges still match. A 3.16 address may be used for 3.41 only where a pin for it passes.
findings.title: OS 3.41 Track Mute Edition is built on OS 3.16

questions.summary: A program loaded from floppy shares RAM with BIOS services it calls, but the full set of BIOS variables is not mapped.
questions.title: What RAM the BIOS uses

questions.summary: The byte layout of the files the MPC3000 saves and loads is not documented here.
questions.title: Disk file formats (SND, PGM, APS, SEQ, ALL, PAR)

questions.summary: DMA channel 2 is wired to IC31, whose function is not identified.
questions.title: What is on DMA channel 2

questions.summary: The BIOS writes ports C010h and C011h around interrupts. They are believed to be the on-chip interrupt controller, but this has not been confirmed.
questions.title: Ports C010h and C011h

questions.summary: The text path to the LCD is known. The controller command set as wired on this board, the graphic mode, and four of the eight INT 43h functions are not.
questions.title: LCD controller commands and graphics

questions.summary: Where MIDI bytes are received, parsed and sent inside the OS is not documented.
questions.title: MIDI handling

questions.summary: The battery-backed memory behind page 61 holds settings, but its layout, checksum and the consequences of writing it are unknown.
questions.title: NVRAM layout and what a RAM program may do to it

questions.summary: OS 3.10 is listed in the MAME ROM set but no contributor has had the image, so no finding applies to it.
questions.title: OS 3.10 has not been examined

questions.summary: Stock and modified OS 3.16 have run on hardware only on a machine with a Vailixi 3.50 EPROM. The other EPROM versions, and the load-segment move, are emulator results.
questions.title: OS 3.16 builds on real 3.08, 3.11 and 3.12 EPROMs

questions.summary: OS 3.16's structure, start-up and 111 routines are mapped. Its sequencer, MIDI, most disk code, the Mixer and five of its eight tasks are not.
questions.title: Unmapped areas of OS 3.16

questions.summary: Two places in the OS can write an I/O port taken from a table and might therefore change a page register while the OS runs.
questions.title: Page-register writes at run time

questions.summary: Address decoding on the CPU board is done by PAL devices whose equations have not been read.
questions.title: PAL address decode

findings.summary: At reset the 256 KiB image is at physical 0xC0000. The boot block copies it to RAM and the OS runs there, where seg*16+off equals the file offset for every address in the image. Only the boot block and reset vector run from ROM.
findings.title: How addresses work in OS 2.00 (reset, the RAM copy, segment:offset)

findings.summary: OS 2.00 has two code segments, 0FE9 (0xFE90-0x1FE7F) and 2033 (0x20330-0x2DF2F), around data segments 0000, 1FFE and 2DF3. A recursive disassembly with resolved indirect targets reaches every instruction seen executing in emulator runs. Eleven indirect sites stay unresolved.
findings.title: Segments, code extents and indirect calls in OS 2.00

findings.summary: From OS 2.00's own code. Floppies use 1 KiB blocks, header and FAT at block 0, a 510-entry directory at block 5. Hard disks use 8 KiB blocks, back-to-back partitions, each with a summed header, 100-volume table and FAT. Not compared with a disk a real unit wrote.
findings.title: Floppy and hard-disk layouts as OS 2.00 reads and writes them

sources: MAME src/mame/akai/s3000.cpp at commit c2caa8969adb (ROM_START s3000)
findings.summary: OS 2.00 is two 128 KiB 27C010 EPROMs, LOW even bytes and HIGH odd. The pair equals MAME's s3000 v2.0 set. The labels 9C79/2900 are chip byte sums. Nothing in the firmware checks the ROM, so a patched image needs no checksum repair.
findings.title: The OS 2.00 EPROM pair, how to identify it, and why it has no ROM checksum

sources: MAME src/mame/akai/s3000.cpp at commit c2caa8969adb (2026-11-13), driver flagged MACHINE_NOT_WORKING
findings.summary: Chips, buses and options of the S3000 family from MAME's driver. MAME says the S3200 uses the XL board, but the only OS image studied here is the S3000-board 256 KiB pair. Read this before assuming any map applies to an S3200.
findings.title: S3200 hardware overview, and why the board type is in doubt

findings.summary: The zero ranges 0x8060-0xFE8F and 0x352DB-0x3FFEF are run-time buffers, not free space. DGROUP variables start near 0x6AE0. Code segment 2033 holds variables at 0x24E4B and 0x2A961. No byte of the OS image has been shown free on hardware.
findings.title: What OS 2.00 writes at run time, and why its zero areas are not free space

findings.summary: At power-on OS 2.00 loads a type-0x63 OS file from floppy, else hard disk partition A volume 1, if its directory version word is at least 0x0C00 (2.00). The file is the raw 256 KiB image, read to 0x50000 and copied down. No content check. Not run on hardware.
findings.title: Loading and saving the OS from disk, and the power-on autoload

findings.summary: OS 2.00 uses the V53's on-chip units at I/O 0xC000-0xC03F (interrupt controller 0xC010, serial 0xC020, timer 0xC030), with INT 8 serial receive, INT 9 tick and INT 11 floppy. MAME puts MIDI on that serial unit. The SIMM-ID probe at 0x20F08 matches MAME's table.
findings.title: Peripheral set-up in OS 2.00 (V53 units, interrupts, serial/MIDI, memory ID)

findings.summary: ROM entry DFE8:00D1 (file 0x1FF51) receives two count-prefixed blocks on the serial unit at 0xC020, echoing each byte, into logical 0x00000-0x1FFFF, then jumps to 0000:0000. No caller of its only jump (0x192C6) is known. Its purpose is not established.
findings.title: The second ROM entry DFE8:00D1, a serial byte loader

firmware.label: OS 2.00 EPROM pair labelled for the S3000 and S3200 (MAME's s3000 'ver 2.0' set)
firmware.notes: The chip files are byte-identical to MAME's s3000 ROM set 'akai s3x00 v2.0 low/high' (same CRC32 and SHA-1). The 16-bit byte sum of each chip equals its label: LOW 9C79, HIGH 2900. The image's own version bytes give 2.00. The image contains the string 'S3000' and S2800 messages but no 'S3200' string. Every code-level finding in this folder is keyed to this image.
firmware.obtain: Read the two 27C010 OS EPROMs of a machine you own and interleave them (LOW = even bytes). Check the hashes below before using any address in this folder.
firmware.source: Computed from the contributor's chip files on 2026-11-13; chip CRC32 and SHA-1 compared with MAME src/mame/akai/s3000.cpp at commit c2caa8969adb.

Akai S950 Operator's Manual (106 pp., as hosted on s950fx.com), Overview and Disk chapters
findings.summary: The S950 service manual's parts lists name every main chip. They agree with MAME's driver - V30, three uPD71071 DMA, uPD71059 ICU, 6850 MIDI ACIA, uPD72066 FDC, 8254/8253 timers - and add the board, EPROM, DRAM, panel PPI and LCD part numbers.
findings.title: S950 hardware from Akai's service manual and owner's manual

sources: Akai S950 Schematic Diagrams and PC Boards: CPU PCB (1/2) No. 6-2 L601302M and CPU PCB (2/2) No. 6-3 L601303M (scanned; as hosted on s950fx.com, downloaded 2026-11-13)
findings.summary: The CPU sees four banked 64 KiB RAM windows (0x00000-0x3FFFF, repeated at 0x40000) and the 64 KiB OS ROM at 0x80000-0xFFFFF. Bank registers at I/O 0x1C0-0x1C6 drive physical A16-A23. Three 74HC138s decode I/O; every select matches MAME.
findings.title: S950 memory map, RAM mapper and I/O decode from Akai's schematics

sources: MAME src/mame/akai/s900.cpp at commit c2caa8969adb (ROM sets)
findings.summary: S950 OS sets 1.0a and 1.2b published on s950fx.com equal MAME's. The "1.2A" files there have MAME's 1.2a LS chip but a different MS chip - 1.0a with 23 bytes changed. All sets reset to JMP FAR F000:FF80. 1.2b identifies itself as "1.5" in one string.
findings.title: S950 OS EPROM images - identity, reset vector, and the two different "1.2a" sets

firmware.label: OS 1.2 EPROM pair published on s950fx.com as V1.2A (MS chip differs from MAME's 1.2a)
firmware.notes: LS chip equals MAME's 1.2a LS chip; MS chip (crc32 2d96a2fb) does not match MAME's (e14ceba2). The linear image is s950-v1.0a with 23 bytes changed (version digit 0 -> 2 at 0x2BDD and 0x9FC0, a 14-byte routine at 0x004A-0x0057 in zero space, a patched sequence at 0x8693-0x8698, one byte at 0x3A0D). Which set Akai shipped as 1.2a is open: see findings/rom-images.md.

firmware.source: Computed on 2026-11-13 from Akai-S950-ROM-V1.2A.zip on s950fx.com (S950-V1.2A-L.BIN, S950-V1.2A-M.BIN).

firmware.notes: Mike Feedback's real-time processing OS. Files: S950FX (type M, block 4), CONFIG (type C, 1,000 bytes, block 68), S950COPY (type M, block 69). The 1.6 MB HD image of the same release has sha256 810215c3fe0d0936bfa26ed83745af0a5184942e56a47655425305508a54b8aa. Only the disk layout is described here; the program was not examined.

machines.summary: Hardware from MAME and Akai's service manual parts lists; ROM 1.0a and 1.2b whole-image hashes checked against dumps, and a second, different '1.2a' set found. Booting a replacement OS from floppy or SCSI is documented (S950FX). Nothing about the OS code is published.
